suggestions.text: The bucket is versioned. If the same key is uploaded again between SEP-1 and SEP-2, a plain DeleteObject puts a delete marker on top of the NEW version, so a fresh upload disappears until someone notices. The second event then finds the source gone and is skipped.
suggestions.proposal: SEP-1 stores the source VersionId from HeadObject in vars.source_version_id. SEP-2 becomes custom code: head the source and delete only when the current VersionId equals vars.source_version_id (DeleteObject with that VersionId). Otherwise it leaves the object alone and logs a WARNING (the new upload has its own event). The uses: s3.delete entry would be dropped.

suggestions.text: staging_prefix stays 'staging_test/' in every environment (Q-ENV-1 got no answer, so the owner's value is kept).
suggestions.proposal: Set staging_prefix to 'staging/' in dev, test and prod, and update the lifecycle rule to match.

suggestions.text: The S3 notification is shared with an existing QueueConfiguration whose filter is unknown. A wrong overlap makes PutBucketNotificationConfiguration fail.
suggestions.proposal: The IaC deployment fails with a clear message when an existing rule overlaps prefix {incoming_prefix} / suffix .zip, so the owner can apply the Q-TRG-1 decision before anything is changed.

units.title: Copy and rename the package
units.does: Check whether the package's source object (ctx.source.key) exists. If it does: compute its sha256 and look for the delivery index object {index_prefix}{stem}/{source_sha256}_{source_key_hash}.json. When the index exists, its source_key equals the source key, and the referenced outgoing object still exists with metadata pkf-source-sha256 equal to the sha: delete the incoming original and mark the package skipped. Otherwise server-side copy the source to {processing_prefix}{stem}_{package_ts}.zip in {source_bucket}, verified by size and sha256 (skip_identical). If the source is gone: resume from an existing processing copy, else skip with a WARNING (replay).
reads: target_bucket:{outgoing_prefix}*_{stem}.zip (head only, the key from the index)
writes: delete source_bucket:{source.key} (only on a verified earlier delivery)
units.idempotency: verified_copy with if_exists=skip_identical: a target with the same sha counts as done, a different sha raises DataError. When the source is already gone, the existing processing copy is resumed; with no processing copy either, the package is skipped.
side_effects: may delete the incoming original when the index proves an earlier verified delivery

clauses.text: The processing key is {processing_prefix}{stem}_{package_ts}.zip, where package_ts is the S3 event time in YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ UTC.
The copy is verified by size and sha256, never by ETag. A different existing target raises DataError.

A package counts as already delivered only when the index object for (stem, source sha256, source key hash) exists, its source_key equals ctx.source.key, and its outgoing object exists with pkf-source-sha256 == source sha256. Then the original is deleted and status=skipped.
Source gone + processing copy present → resume. Source gone + no processing copy → status skipped with a WARNING (message is deleted by ack).
When the current source size differs from ctx.source.size, log a WARNING and process the current version.

helpers.name: source_key_hash
helpers.purpose: stable short hash of the source key for the index name

helpers.name: index_key
helpers.signature: def index_key(rt: Runtime, stem: str, sha: str, key_hash: str) -> str

units.pseudocode:
1. s3 = rt.s3(); src_b = ctx.source.bucket; src_k = ctx.source.key; stem = ctx.vars['stem']; ts = ctx.vars['package_ts'].
2. proc_key = check_key(f"{rt.settings['processing_prefix']}{stem}_{ts}.zip"); kh = source_key_hash(src_k).
3. h = head(s3, src_b, src_k).
4. If h is None:
   a. ph = head(s3, rt.settings['source_bucket'], proc_key). If ph: sha = sha256_of(s3, source_bucket, proc_key); set vars source_sha256=sha, source_key_hash=kh, source_key=src_k; artefacts.renamed_key=proc_key; log INFO 'resume'; return ctx.
   b. Else log WARNING 'source gone, nothing to resume'; ctx.status='skipped'; return ctx.
5. If ctx.source.size is not None and h['size'] != ctx.source.size: log WARNING.
6. sha = sha256_of(s3, src_b, src_k).
7. ik = index_key(rt, stem, sha, kh); obj = head(s3, target_bucket, ik).
8. If obj: download it to rt.tmpdir() and json-load it → idx. If idx['source_key'] == src_k: oh = head(s3, target_bucket, idx['outgoing_key']). If oh and oh.metadata['pkf-source-sha256'] == sha: delete(s3, src_b, src_k, missing_ok=True); ctx.status='skipped'; vars.already_delivered=idx['outgoing_key']; return ctx.
9. verified_copy(s3, src_b, src_k, rt.settings['source_bucket'], proc_key, if_exists='skip_identical') (a different existing sha → DataError).
10. Set vars source_sha256=sha, source_key_hash=kh, source_key=src_k; artefacts.renamed_key=proc_key; return ctx.

units.title: Remove the original
units.does: Delete the package's own source object (ctx.source.bucket/ctx.source.key, the exact key from the event). An object that is already gone is fine. It runs only when SEP-1 left status ok, which means the processing copy is verified (skipped packages pass through).
units.idempotency: missing_ok=true: a second run finds the object gone and does nothing.
side_effects: adds a delete marker (versioned bucket); the noncurrent version expires after 30 days via the lifecycle rule

clauses.text: Delete the source only after SEP-1 verified the processing copy (guaranteed by the order and status ok).
bucket/key default to ctx.source; the owner's '{incoming_prefix}{name}.zip' template is replaced because {name} already holds '.zip'.

units.pseudocode:
1. run_op('s3.delete', ctx, rt, {'missing_ok': True}): delete ctx.source.bucket/ctx.source.key.
2. Return ctx.

units.title: Build the manifest
units.does: Unless a staging zip for this package already exists with matching pkf-source-sha256: check free disk space, then download artefacts.renamed_key to rt.shared_dir() and safe-extract it. Build manifest.csv with columns file_name,size_bytes (header row; one row per non-folder entry in zip order; file_name is the path inside the zip, size_bytes the uncompressed size). Build a new zip64 with the original files plus manifest.csv at the root. Hand over its path in artefacts.new_zip_path.
units.idempotency: When the staging zip already exists with pkf-source-sha256 == vars.source_sha256, it sets artefacts.staging_key and builds nothing; a staging zip with a different source sha raises DataError. Otherwise it is a pure local rebuild in shared_dir.
side_effects: local files in rt.shared_dir() (deleted after the TRN group)

clauses.text: manifest.csv: UTF-8 without BOM, comma separator, RFC 4180 quoting, LF line endings, header file_name,size_bytes, rows in zip entry order, every non-folder entry (not only .pdf).
A zip that already contains a root manifest.csv fails the package with DataError.
Extraction uses archive.safe_extract (zip-slip, symlinks and bombs → DataError).
Before downloading, free space in shared_dir must be ≥ 3 × zip size × 1.1, else TransientError.
TRN-1 and TRN-2 share one Airflow task (group); the local zip path is handed over in artefacts.new_zip_path.

helpers.name: build_manifest
helpers.signature: def build_manifest(entries: list[dict], dest: Path) -> Path
helpers.pseudocode: rows=[(e['name'], e['size']) for e in entries if not e['is_dir']]; open dest 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline=''; csv.writer(f, lineterminator='\n', quoting=csv.QUOTE_MINIMAL); writerow(['file_name','size_bytes']); writerows(rows); return dest

helpers.name: ensure_disk
helpers.signature: def ensure_disk(path: Path, zip_size: int) -> None
helpers.pseudocode: free=shutil.disk_usage(path).free; if free < int(zip_size*3*1.1): raise TransientError(f'need {..} bytes, free {free}')

units.pseudocode:
1. s3=rt.s3(); stem, ts = vars; stg_key = check_key(f"{rt.settings['staging_prefix']}{stem}_{ts}.zip").
2. sh = head(s3, target_bucket, stg_key). If sh: if sh.metadata.get('pkf-source-sha256') == vars.source_sha256: artefacts.staging_key=stg_key; vars.staged=True; return ctx. Else raise DataError('staging object exists for another source').
3. d = rt.shared_dir(); ph = head(s3, source_bucket, artefacts.renamed_key); ensure_disk(d, ph['size']).
4. zp = download(s3, source_bucket, artefacts.renamed_key, d/'in.zip').
5. ents = entries(zp); if any(e['name']=='manifest.csv' for e in ents): raise DataError.
6. files = safe_extract(zp, d/'x'); map each entry name to d/'x'/name.
7. m = build_manifest(ents, d/'manifest.csv').
8. out = make_zip([(d/'x'/e['name'], e['name']) for e in ents if not e['is_dir']] + [(m,'manifest.csv')], d/'out.zip').
9. Delete in.zip to free space; artefacts.new_zip_path=str(out); vars.manifest_rows=len(non-folder entries); return ctx.

units.title: Upload to staging
units.does: Upload artefacts.new_zip_path to {staging_prefix}{stem}_{package_ts}.zip in {target_bucket}, with metadata pkf-source-key=vars.source_key and pkf-source-sha256=vars.source_sha256 (pkf-sha256 is added by the kit), if_exists=fail. Hand over the key as artefacts.staging_key. When TRN-1 found the staging zip already done (vars.staged), do nothing.
units.idempotency: TRN-1 detects an existing staging zip for the same source sha and sets vars.staged, so the upload is skipped. Written under the final name only.

clauses.text: The staging zip carries user metadata pkf-source-key and pkf-source-sha256.
artefacts.staging_key is set in every ok path.

units.pseudocode:
1. If vars.get('staged'): return ctx (staging_key already set).
2. key = check_key(f"{rt.settings['staging_prefix']}{vars.stem}_{vars.package_ts}.zip").
3. upload(rt.s3(), Path(artefacts.new_zip_path), target_bucket, key, if_exists='fail', metadata={'pkf-source-key': vars.source_key, 'pkf-source-sha256': vars.source_sha256}).
4. artefacts.staging_key = key; return ctx.

units.title: Deliver to outgoing
units.does: Verified server-side copy of artefacts.staging_key to {outgoing_prefix}{package_ts}_{stem}.zip in {target_bucket} with if_exists=skip_identical (never overwrite; a different existing object raises DataError). Then check that the outgoing object carries pkf-source-key and pkf-source-sha256 equal to the vars. Finally write the delivery index object {index_prefix}{stem}/{source_sha256}_{source_key_hash}.json.
units.idempotency: skip_identical on both writes. The index content is deterministic (sorted keys, no run clock), so a re-run finds identical objects.

clauses.text: Outgoing name {outgoing_prefix}{package_ts}_{stem}.zip; an existing object is never overwritten.
After the copy, the outgoing metadata pkf-source-key/pkf-source-sha256 must equal vars.source_key/vars.source_sha256, else DataError.
Index JSON = {"source_key", "source_sha256", "outgoing_key", "outgoing_sha256", "package_ts"}, sort_keys, written only after the outgoing object is verified.

units.pseudocode:
1. s3=rt.s3(); tb=rt.settings['target_bucket']; out_key=check_key(f"{outgoing_prefix}{package_ts}_{stem}.zip").
2. r = verified_copy(s3, tb, artefacts.staging_key, tb, out_key, if_exists='skip_identical').
3. oh = head(s3, tb, out_key); if oh.metadata.get('pkf-source-key')!=vars.source_key or oh.metadata.get('pkf-source-sha256')!=vars.source_sha256: raise DataError.
4. idx = {source_key, source_sha256, outgoing_key: out_key, outgoing_sha256: sha256_of(s3,tb,out_key), package_ts}; write json.dumps(idx, sort_keys=True) to rt.tmpdir()/'idx.json'.
5. ik = index_key(rt, stem, source_sha256, source_key_hash); upload(s3, path, tb, ik, if_exists='skip_identical').
6. artefacts.outgoing_key=out_key; artefacts.index_key=ik; return ctx.

units.title: Clean up
units.does: After confirming that artefacts.outgoing_key exists in {target_bucket}, delete artefacts.renamed_key (processing copy, source_bucket) and artefacts.staging_key (target_bucket), missing_ok. A failure here does not fail the package.
side_effects: delete markers; the lifecycle rule expires the noncurrent versions after 30 days

clauses.text: Delete only when head(outgoing_key) succeeds; otherwise log a WARNING and keep both copies.

units.pseudocode:
1. If head(s3, target_bucket, artefacts.outgoing_key) is None: log WARNING; return ctx.
2. delete(s3, source_bucket, artefacts.renamed_key, missing_ok=True).
3. delete(s3, target_bucket, artefacts.staging_key, missing_ok=True).
4. Return ctx.

s3_objects.meaning: only copy of the package; incoming original deleted

fields.name: artefacts.new_zip_path
fields.meaning: local path in rt.shared_dir() of the rebuilt zip (valid only inside the TRN group); absent when vars.staged

fields.name: vars.staged
fields.meaning: true when the staging zip already existed

s3_objects.meaning: delivered package; processing and staging copies deleted

resources.name: source/target bucket
resources.details: source_bucket and target_bucket are the same bucket. Versioned, SSE-KMS default. SEP-1: Get/Head incoming, index and outgoing; Copy to processing; Delete incoming. SEP-2: Delete incoming. TRN-1: Get processing, Head staging. TRN-2: Put staging. DLP-1: Get staging, Put outgoing and index. DLP-2: Delete processing and staging. Report: Put report_prefix. ListBucket is needed so a HEAD on a missing key returns 404.

resources.name: incoming prefix
resources.details: watched prefix; the pipeline never writes here (no loop)

resources.name: processing prefix
resources.details: SEP-1 writes, TRN-1 reads, DLP-2 deletes

resources.name: staging prefix
resources.details: TRN-2 writes, DLP-1 reads, DLP-2 deletes

resources.name: outgoing prefix
resources.details: DLP-1 writes, SEP-1 heads; never deleted or overwritten

resources.name: package queue
resources.details: visibility timeout 21600 s, retention 4 days, SSE-SQS, redrive to the DLQ maxReceiveCount 3. Policy allows s3.amazonaws.com sqs:SendMessage with aws:SourceArn = the bucket ARN and aws:SourceAccount = aws_account.

resources.name: package DLQ
resources.details: retention 14 days, SSE-SQS; alarm on ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible > 0

resources.name: bucket notification
resources.details: IaC only. Read the existing configuration (1 QueueConfiguration), add s3:ObjectCreated:* with prefix {incoming_prefix} and suffix .zip → queue_url, keep every existing rule. On overlap the owner decides (Q-TRG-1).

resources.name: bucket KMS key
resources.details: bucket default SSE-KMS key (from the probe). No sse param is passed; objects inherit the default encryption.

resources.name: lifecycle rule
resources.details: IaC only (SUG-1). Expire noncurrent versions under incoming_prefix, processing_prefix and staging_prefix after 30 days, and remove expired delete markers; merge with existing rules.

pseudocode_dag:
DAG s3_zip_manifest: schedule '0 * * * *' UTC, catchup=False, max_active_runs=1, dagrun_timeout 5 h (below the 6 h SQS visibility timeout).
start → SEP-0 discover (sqs, queue_url, max_packages 100; drops TestEvents and duplicates) → per package (dynamic task mapping, max 8 parallel): SEP-1 (timeout 60 min) → SEP-2 (10 min) → [TRN-1 + TRN-2 in one Airflow task, shared_dir, timeout 120 min, worker scratch ≥ 8 GiB] → DLP-1 (60 min) → DLP-2 (10 min, on_failure skip) → outcome → DLP-Z ack (delete delivered/skipped handles, release failed) → report (write_uri s3://{target_bucket}/{report_prefix}{run_id}.json; RunFailed when any failed) → end.
Retries: 2 per task, retry_delay 5 min, exponential backoff, only for TransientError and unexpected errors. DataError fails the package without a retry; ConfigError fails the run. E-mail on task failure and on RunFailed to alert_email.
assumptions: Q-TRG-1 accepted: IaC adds one QueueConfiguration (ObjectCreated:*, prefix {incoming_prefix}, suffix .zip) to the new queue and keeps the existing rules; on overlap the owner decides.

Q-SEP-1-1 accepted, combined with SUG-2: dedupe uses the index object {index_prefix}{stem}/{source_sha256}_{source_key_hash}.json written by DLP-1 instead of listing outgoing/. SEP-1 also verifies that the referenced outgoing object still has a matching pkf-source-sha256 before it deletes the original.
SUG-1 accepted: lifecycle rule for noncurrent versions (30 days) under incoming, processing and staging, plus expired delete marker removal.
SUG-3 accepted: report written to s3://{target_bucket}/{report_prefix}{run_id}.json; report_prefix dev value reports/s3_zip_manifest/.
index_prefix dev value 'index/s3_zip_manifest/' is derived (owner named the setting only).

Unanswered non-blocking proposals adopted: Q-SEP-2-1 (s3.delete with defaults, missing_ok), Q-TRN-1-1 (group TRN-1+TRN-2), Q-TRN-1-2 (manifest format; root manifest.csv → DataError), Q-SRC-1 (sub-folders accepted, names by stem; collisions → DataError), Q-SRC-2 (current version, WARNING on size mismatch), Q-SEP-1-2 (replay skip/resume), Q-TRG-2 (DLQ, maxReceiveCount 3, visibility 21600 s, SSE-SQS, queue policy), Q-NF-1 (≥ 8 GiB scratch, 3×size+10% check → TransientError), Q-DLP-1-1 (skip_identical; different sha → DataError).
Q-ENV-1 got no answer: the owner's staging_prefix 'staging_test/' is kept (see SUG-6).
Encryption: no sse param; objects inherit the bucket default SSE-KMS key; IAM grants kms:Decrypt/GenerateDataKey on it.
No loop: the pipeline writes only to processing, staging, outgoing, index and reports, never under incoming/.
Examples 2–4 are derived; example 1 is quoted from SEP-1/TRN-1 (zip contents derived).
